title: This Missouri Airbnb Was Once a Morgue, and It Comes With Ghost-Hunting Gear
excerpt: Missouri's Ozarks are full of charming small-town squares, and Ozark's is one of the prettiest, lined with old storefronts, cafes, and shops.
content:
Missouri's Ozarks are full of charming small-town squares, and Ozark's is one of the prettiest, lined with old storefronts, cafes, and shops. A block away, Church Street Antiques and More looks like the kind of place you'd pop into for a vintage find. But the building has had a few other lives over the past century, and some of them were decidedly darker.

It's been a church, a morgue, a funeral home, and a museum. Today, the back of the building is a loft rental called the Historic Morgue, and the listing makes one thing very clear: there are no refunds if you leave mid-stay because you got scared!

It also landed in Airbnb's haunted stays roundup. Spooky as the premise is, it holds a 4.98 rating across more than 200 reviews and ranks among Airbnb's top 1% of homes.

A Building With Many Past Lives

According to KY3, the building went up in the early 1900s as a Methodist church before becoming a Presbyterian church and morgue. In 1920, it became the Ozark Undertaking Company, and it later operated as a funeral home. "They had all of the afterlife services right here at this location," owner Alta Bivens told KY3.

The listing calls it a nationally recognized historic building. As Alta learned more about its history, people kept asking whether they could spend the night, so she turned the front into an antique shop and opened the back as an Airbnb.

What to Expect Inside the Historic Morgue

The decor leans fully into the building's past. You'll find antiques with a modern twist and morgue-inspired touches throughout, which the listing describes as paying homage to its dark history.

The loft is one open room with a king bed, a full bed, a twin, and an antique settee, sleeping up to six. The kitchen is surprisingly roomy, with a triple-basin sink, new stainless steel appliances including a gas stove, a small breakfast bar and a large table for group meals.

The bathroom might be the highlight. It pairs an early-1900s clawfoot tub with a brand-new modern shower and an antique vanity basin.

Out back, a privacy-fenced yard with seating and solar string lights is yours alone. The building's former sanctuary and basement are closed off to guests, so you'll have the loft, kitchen, bathroom, and yard to yourself.

Bring Your Ghost-Hunting Nerve

Here's where things get interesting. The host provides paranormal research equipment for guests, including a spirit box, an EMF detector, and dowsing rods.

The listing says numerous professional paranormal teams have spent the night and reported unexplained events. Alta told KY3 that she once felt an entire hand resting on her back inside the rental, and people have reported seeing a woman peering out of the windows.

Still, she approaches it all with a healthy dose of skepticism. "I'm a believer, but I'm also a skeptic," she told KY3. "So I want to debunk everything that comes up to be certain."

The listing notes there's no guarantee you'll experience anything, and that the stay and some decor may not suit children or every adult. If you love a good ghost story, that's half the fun.

Exploring Ozark

You're steps from Ozark's downtown square, with shops, restaurants, and cafes all within walking distance. The Finley River and its park are a short walk away, and Finley Farms and the historic Ozark Mill are close by for an afternoon out.

Springfield is just to the north and Branson to the south. Table Rock Lake and the area's amusement parks are within about 30 minutes. Here are some things to do in Branson if you'd like to make a weekend of it.

Can't get enough haunted history? Add another night at Missouri's haunted Hotel Bothwell or the haunted Walnut Street Inn. Visiting in autumn? Here are more fall things to do in Missouri.

Plan Your Stay

The Airbnb listing for the Historic Morgue books through Airbnb, and the exact address is shared once you reserve. Check-in is self-serve with a smart lock, and parking is free, with street parking nearby.

Host Alta-Ann is a Superhost with seven years of hosting, and guests often mention her personalized welcome touches. Pets are allowed, and the loft runs cool, so the host asks guests to keep the thermostat between 68 and 73 degrees.

Check the listing for current rates and availability. October books up fast for obvious reasons, but the morgue's history doesn't take a day off the rest of the year.

The loft has a king bed, a full, a twin, and an antique settee, all in one room. Antique decor with a modern twist runs throughout, and Airbnb ranks it among its top 5% of homes.

Before You Book

Ozark sits between Springfield and Branson. Smallin Civil War Cave and Finley Farms are nearby if you want daytime plans. The Airbnb listing keeps the exact location private until booking. For daytime plans, see these fall things to do in Missouri.
